For a safe jump, swing the arms, push off with both feet and land softly with bent knees, feet about shoulder-width apart and arms forward for balance. Warm up first, choose a clear, flat space and stop if anything hurts.

lesson.guided_practice:
PRACTISE BEFORE READING THE FEEDBACK
Mei jumps over a line, lands with straight legs and falls backwards. Write two cues that would fix her landing and say why they protect her body.

FEEDBACK
Cues: 'bend your knees' and 'land with feet apart and arms forward'. Bent knees absorb the force like springs, and wide feet and forward arms keep balance. Stiff, straight legs send the impact into the knees and back.

WATCH FOR
Thinking the farthest jump is the best jump. A strong jump has good technique and a balanced landing; distance improves with practice.
lesson.independent_task:
INDEPENDENT EVIDENCE
Set up a safe, clear space with a start line. Practise ten standing jumps and a short run using your own cue words. Use a recording sheet to rate your technique (arms, knees, landing) from 1 to 3 and set one goal. Skip jumping if you have any pain.

Write a short reflection naming one choice you changed and why. Any movement is optional, adult-supervised and can be done in a gentler way or described instead.

teaching.guided_attempt: Describe or practise one fresh situation that uses the same skill and write a short reason for your choice.
teaching.misconception: Repeating the worked example cannot show transfer to a new situation.
teaching.model: Running, jumping and landing are fundamental movement skills. Good running has bent arms swinging opposite to the legs, eyes forward and landing on the balls of the feet. For a safe jump, swing the arms, push off with both feet and land softly with bent knees, feet about shoulder-width apart and arms forward for balance. Warm up first, choose a clear, flat space and stop if anything hurts. Now choose a different situation to show you can transfer the idea.
teaching.rule: Use the same PDHPE idea in a new place, game or situation, not a copy of the example. Review safety, fairness and inclusion.
teaching.why: This helps the learner make safe, healthy and respectful choices using clear cues and reasons, rather than guessing or copying others. Every choice keeps bodies safe and includes everyone.
